title: Disentangling Task Difficulty from Run-Level Failure in Agent Failure Prediction
title_zh: 将任务难度与运行级失败在智能体失败预测中解耦

paragraphs.en: Predicting whether an LLM agent will eventually fail has emerged as a promising direction for supporting intervention during agent’s run. Recent approaches report strong predictive performance, often with AUROC values between 0.85 0.85 and 0.94 0.94 . However, the predictors are typically trained combining agent’s runs (also called, trajectories or traces) from many different tasks. We hypothesized that the strong performance may come partly from recognizing that some tasks are harder than others, rather than from detecting whether a particular run is heading toward failure. This distinction matters operationally because task-level difficulty supports decisions about where to allocate computation, whereas run-level failure prediction is needed to decide whether to intervene in an ongoing trajectory. To disentangle task-level difficulty from run-level failure signals, we conducted a study to analyze benchmarks containing repeated attempts of the same task by the same LLM agent. We separate comparisons across different agents and task units from comparisons between successful and failed runs of the same unit. Across the evaluated corpora, pooled AUROC is dominated by comparisons across different agent–task units: more than 99.93% of the underlying positive–negative pairs are cross-unit. Accordingly, predictors that never observe the current run can achieve high pooled performance, including a difficulty oracle with AUROC up to 0.945, while remaining at chance within task. This means that strong pooled performance may be more informative for deciding where to allocate computation than for deciding whether to intervene in a particular run. In contrast, early run-level discrimination is consistently weak across trajectory predictors, published and released monitors, and hidden-state probes, although it improves later in run and is stronger for weaker agents. Consistent with this distinction, under fixed token budgets, task-level allocation outperforms abort-only strategies, while early stopping becomes beneficial only when within-task AUROC reaches roughly 0.84–0.93, far above the 0.50–0.55 range observed for early monitors. These findings highlight that failure prediction should be evaluated not only by how accurately it predicts outcomes, but by whether the captured signal supports the deployment decision the predictor is intended to make.

paragraphs.en: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents increasingly support multi-step tasks in software engineering and other domains ( Liu et al., 2026 ; Jin et al., 2024 ) . Unlike conventional LLM applications that primarily generate a response from a fixed input context, LLM-based agents operate through multi-step interactions in which they take actions, invoke tools, and incorporate observations from the environment while attempting to complete a task ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Yang et al., 2024 ) . This increased autonomy enables agents to solve complex problems, but it also introduces substantial execution risk. Recent studies report failure rates ranging from 41 % 41\% to 86.7 % 86.7\% across seven agentic frameworks ( Cemri et al., 2025 ) . Such failures are costly because an unsuccessful run may consume considerable time, tokens, and computational resources before its eventual outcome becomes known ( Du et al., 2026 ; Bai et al., 2026 ; Khanna, 2026 ) . These costs have motivated growing interest in agent failure prediction : determining, during execution, whether an ongoing agent run is likely to fail ( Barke et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) . An accurate failure predictor could support early intervention and avoid wasting resources. For example, by terminating an unpromising execution, requesting human assistance, or changing the agent’s strategy before additional resources are consumed.

paragraphs.en: Existing work commonly formulates the prediction problem as trajectory classification ( Vasudev et al., 2026 ; Shi et al., 2026 ; Cho et al., 2026 ) . They collect successful and failed agent trajectories, train predictors on their trajectories, and use the resulting models to estimate the failure risk of new runs while they are still in progress. These predictors are commonly evaluated using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC), which measures how well a predictor discriminates failed executions from successful ones ( Vasudev et al., 2026 ; Cho et al., 2026 ) . Within a benchmark and evaluation condition, a common practice is to pool predictions from executions of different task instances and compute AUROC over the resulting successful and failed runs ( Cho et al., 2026 ; Vasudev et al., 2026 ; Pham et al., 2026 ) . We refer to this aggregate measure as pooled AUROC . High pooled AUROC values are commonly interpreted as evidence that a predictor can identify executions that are likely to fail. However, this interpretation overlooks an important possibility: the predictor may distinguish tasks with different baseline failure rates rather than distinguish successful and failed executions of the same task .

paragraphs.en: This distinction matters because agent outcomes depend on both the task and the particular execution ( Bjarnason et al., 2026 ; Krsteski and Meyer, 2026 ; Lee, 2026 ) . Some tasks may fail substantially more often than others. When runs from many tasks are pooled together, a predictor can therefore obtain a high AUROC by assigning higher failure scores to tasks with high baseline failure rates and lower scores to tasks with low baseline failure rates ( Janes et al., 2009 ; Borkan et al., 2019 ) . Such a predictor can rank failures above successes across the benchmark even if it cannot distinguish a successful run from a failed run of the same task . Evidence from prior work suggests that this possibility is realistic. A predictor of task success before execution begins , using only static task properties, reaches AUROC of 0.841 0.841 on held-out SWE-bench Verified instances ( Ge et al., 2026 ) , within the range reported by systems that observe agent trajectories heavily. This does not imply that trajectories contain no useful information. Rather, it exposes an ambiguity in pooled evaluation: strong discrimination may arise from between-task differences, run-specific execution signals, or both. Conflating task-level difficulty and run-level failure can therefore misrepresent a predictor’s suitability for runtime intervention. Task-level difficulty can help determine where to allocate computation, which LLM to use, or whether a task should be attempted. A runtime monitor must answer a different question: given that the agent is already executing this task, does the evidence from this particular run indicate that it is heading toward failure? The latter decision requires information that separates different outcomes of the same task.
paragraphs.zh: 这种区分之所以重要，是因为智能体的结果既取决于任务本身，也取决于具体的执行过程（Bjarnason 等，2026；Krsteski 和 Meyer，2026；Lee，2026）。 某些任务失败的概率可能远高于其他任务。 因此，当来自多个任务的运行结果被汇总在一起时，预测模型可以通过为基线失败率高的任务分配更高的失败分数，而为基线失败率低的任务分配更低的分数，从而获得较高的 AUROC（Janes 等，2009；Borkan 等，2019）。 即使该预测模型无法区分同一任务中成功运行与失败运行的差异，它仍然可以在基准测试中将所有失败案例排在成功案例之前。 以往研究的证据表明，这种可能性是现实存在的。 一种仅基于静态任务属性、在运行开始前对任务成功进行预测的模型，在预留的 SWE-bench Verified 实例上达到了 0.841 的 AUROC（Ge 等，2026），这一数值处于那些大量观察智能体轨迹的系统所报告的范围之内。 但这并不意味着轨迹中不包含任何有用信息。 相反，这揭示了汇总评估中的一个模糊性：较强的区分能力可能源于任务间的差异、特定运行的执行信号，或是两者共同作用的结果。 因此，将任务层面的难度与运行层面的失败混为一谈，可能会错误地反映该预测模型在运行时干预方面的适用性。 任务层面的难度有助于决定计算资源应分配何处、使用哪个 LLM，或者是否应该尝试执行某个任务。 运行时监控器必须回答一个不同的问题：既然智能体已经在执行该任务，那么本次特定运行的证据是否表明其正走向失败？ 后一种决策需要能够区分同一任务不同结果的信息。

sents.en: Such a predictor can rank failures above successes across the benchmark even if it cannot distinguish a successful run from a failed run of the same task .
sents.zh: 即使该预测模型无法区分同一任务中成功运行与失败运行的差异，它仍然可以在基准测试中将所有失败案例排在成功案例之前。

sents.en: Evidence from prior work suggests that this possibility is realistic.
sents.zh: 以往研究的证据表明，这种可能性是现实存在的。

sents.en: A predictor of task success before execution begins , using only static task properties, reaches AUROC of 0.841 0.841 on held-out SWE-bench Verified instances ( Ge et al., 2026 ) , within the range reported by systems that observe agent trajectories heavily.
sents.zh: 一种仅基于静态任务属性、在运行开始前对任务成功进行预测的模型，在预留的 SWE-bench Verified 实例上达到了 0.841 的 AUROC（Ge 等，2026），这一数值处于那些大量观察智能体轨迹的系统所报告的范围之内。

sents.en: This does not imply that trajectories contain no useful information.
sents.zh: 但这并不意味着轨迹中不包含任何有用信息。

sents.en: Rather, it exposes an ambiguity in pooled evaluation: strong discrimination may arise from between-task differences, run-specific execution signals, or both.
sents.zh: 相反，这揭示了汇总评估中的一个模糊性：较强的区分能力可能源于任务间的差异、特定运行的执行信号，或是两者共同作用的结果。

sents.en: Conflating task-level difficulty and run-level failure can therefore misrepresent a predictor’s suitability for runtime intervention.
sents.zh: 因此，将任务层面的难度与运行层面的失败混为一谈，可能会错误地反映该预测模型在运行时干预方面的适用性。

sents.en: Task-level difficulty can help determine where to allocate computation, which LLM to use, or whether a task should be attempted.
sents.zh: 任务层面的难度有助于决定计算资源应分配何处、使用哪个 LLM，或者是否应该尝试执行某个任务。

sents.en: A runtime monitor must answer a different question: given that the agent is already executing this task, does the evidence from this particular run indicate that it is heading toward failure?
sents.zh: 运行时监控器必须回答一个不同的问题：既然智能体已经在执行该任务，那么本次特定运行的证据是否表明其正走向失败？

sents.en: The latter decision requires information that separates different outcomes of the same task.
sents.zh: 后一种决策需要能够区分同一任务不同结果的信息。

paragraphs.en: Our study investigates how strongly the distinction between task-level difficulty and run-level failure affects the evaluation and use of agent failure predictors. Building on the distinction between pooled and conditional discrimination studied in statistics ( Pepe, 2003 ; Janes and Pepe, 2009 ) and recent evidence of task-level confounds in agent evaluation ( Mehtiyev and Assunção, 2026 ; Bulut, 2026 ) , we ask three questions: (RQ1) how much reported predictive performance reflects differences between tasks rather than the state of the current execution, (RQ2) whether run-specific signals are available early enough to support intervention, and (RQ3) whether separating these signals changes the deployment decisions suggested by failure predictors. To answer these questions, we exploit repeated agent executions, in which a fixed agent configuration attempts the same task multiple times. Because the task and agent remain constant while the execution varies, successful and failed attempts within the same model–task unit provide a setting for isolating run-level discrimination from between-unit differences. We analyze repeated-attempt corpora from SWE-agent ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , SWE-rebench ( Badertdinov et al., 2025 ) , LiveClawBench ( Long et al., 2026 ) , and Latent Programming Horizons ( Silva et al., 2026 ) , spanning different agent scaffolds, models, and domains. Empirically, we decompose pooled AUROC into within-unit and cross-unit comparisons; compare run-blind baselines with trajectory-based predictors, published and released monitoring systems, and hidden-state probes at online-computable execution prefixes; and measure within-task discrimination while holding the task and acting model fixed. Finally, we evaluate the practical consequences of these signals through replay experiments under fixed token budgets, comparing task-level resource allocation, run-level aborting, and their combination.

paragraphs.en: Our results reveal a consistent progression across the three research questions. For RQ1, we find that pooled AUROC is dominated by cross-unit comparisons: more than 99.93% of the underlying positive–negative pairs compare different model–task units, allowing a difficulty oracle to reach pooled AUROC of 0.945 while remaining at 0.500 within task. For RQ2, early run-level discrimination is consistently weak across trajectory-based predictors, published and released monitoring systems, and hidden-state probes, although the signal becomes stronger later in execution and is more pronounced for weaker agents. For RQ3, this distinction changes the practical value of prediction: under fixed token budgets, task-level allocation outperforms abort-only strategies, while run-level monitoring becomes beneficial only when within-task AUROC reaches roughly 0.84–0.93, far above the 0.50–0.55 range observed for early monitors. paragraphs.en: Taken together, our contributions change how failure-prediction performance should be interpreted for LLM agents. A high pooled AUROC can be useful evidence that failures are associated with predictable differences across tasks, but it does not by itself establish that a monitor can recognize which particular execution of a task will fail. The distinction matters operationally: task-level information supports decisions about where to spend computation , whereas run-level information supports decisions about whether to stop the execution currently in progress .
paragraphs.zh: 综合来看，我们的研究贡献改变了人们对 LLM 智能体故障预测性能的解释方式。 较高的合并 AUROC 值可以作为有效证据，表明故障与不同任务间可预测的差异相关，但它本身并不能证明监控器能够识别出具体哪项任务执行会失败。 这种区别在操作层面具有重要意义：任务级的信息有助于决定将计算资源分配到哪里，而运行级的信息则有助于决定是否停止当前正在进行的执行过程。

paragraphs.en: Consider two SWE-bench Verified tasks from Django, each attempted ten times by the same agent and model. This gives 20 20 runs in total. The agent solves django-10914 nine times but solves django-10973 only once. Now consider a predictor that never observes the trajectory and simply assigns each task its observed failure rate: 0.1 0.1 for every run of the first task and 0.9 0.9 for every run of the second. Evaluated across all 20 20 runs, this predictor achieves AUROC 0.900 0.900 . In either task, however, its AUROC is exactly 0.500 0.500 because every attempt at the same task receives the same score. The predictor therefore distinguishes which task is harder, but not which particular run will fail. At benchmark scale, this distinction becomes substantial: in C4-L (presented in Table 1 ), only about 0.07 % 0.07\% of the comparisons underlying pooled AUROC come from runs of the same task. This helps explain why strong pooled performance can coexist with weak run-level discrimination, and why task-level information may be more useful for allocating computation than for deciding whether to abort the current run.

sents.zh: 在所有 20 次运行中评估后，该预测器的 AUROC 达到 0.900。

sents.en: In either task, however, its AUROC is exactly 0.500 0.500 because every attempt at the same task receives the same score.
sents.zh: 然而，在任一任务中，其 AUROC 恰好为 0.500，因为对同一任务的每次尝试都获得了相同的分数。

sents.en: The predictor therefore distinguishes which task is harder, but not which particular run will fail.
sents.zh: 因此，该预测器能够区分哪个任务更难，但无法区分哪次特定的运行会失败。

sents.en: At benchmark scale, this distinction becomes substantial: in C4-L (presented in Table 1 ), only about 0.07 % 0.07\% of the comparisons underlying pooled AUROC come from runs of the same task.
sents.zh: 在基准规模上，这种区别变得显著：在 C4-L（见表格 1）中，汇总 AUROC 所依据的比较中，只有约 0.07% 来自同一任务的多次运行。

sents.en: This helps explain why strong pooled performance can coexist with weak run-level discrimination, and why task-level information may be more useful for allocating computation than for deciding whether to abort the current run.
sents.zh: 这有助于解释为何强大的汇总性能可以与较弱的运行级区分能力共存，以及为何任务级信息在分配计算资源时可能比决定是否中止当前运行更有用。

paragraphs.en: Research on agent failure prediction spans three questions: what makes a task likely to fail before execution, what an ongoing trajectory reveals about its eventual outcome, and whether acting on a prediction improves system behavior. These questions rely on different information and support different decisions. Several runtime predictors evaluate executions from multiple tasks together ( Cho et al., 2026 ; Vasudev et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) , potentially mixing task-level difficulty with run-specific failure signals. We review these lines of work to clarify what existing evaluations establish about run-level monitoring.

paragraphs.en: Pre-execution prediction is well established in software engineering, from defect-risk estimation using static software features ( EsfandyariDoulabi et al., 2025 ) to LLM reliability analyses showing sensitivity to task difficulty and repeated evaluation ( Sun et al., 2026 ) . More directly, Ge et al. ( Ge et al., 2026 ) estimate agent task difficulty using Item Response Theory (IRT) and task features. Their model reaches AUROC 0.841 0.841 on held-out SWE-bench Verified tasks, while a problem-statement-only variant reaches 0.786 0.786 , showing that substantial discrimination is possible before observing the current execution. Krsteski and Meyer ( Krsteski and Meyer, 2026 ) similarly predict IRT-derived difficulty across 17 agentic benchmarks and show that aggregate AUC can remain high even when task-level scores do not distinguish individual outcomes. Our work, in contrast, asks whether high aggregate failure-prediction performance also captures run-specific information within repeated attempts of the same model–task pair, and whether task-level and run-level signals support different deployment decisions.

paragraphs.en: Mehtiyev and Assunção ( Mehtiyev and Assunção, 2026 ) further show that trajectory-based associations depend on what is held fixed. Across 9,374 coding-agent trajectories, failed runs are longer when outcomes are compared within an agent, whereas the relationship often reverses when different agents are compared on the same task. Their results highlight the importance of conditioning when interpreting trajectory-level associations. We extend this idea by holding both the acting model and task fixed, allowing direct measurement of discrimination between successful and failed executions of the same model–task unit. Bulut ( Bulut, 2026 ) provides the closest measurement precedent to our study. In LLM reasoning trajectories, Bulut shows that pooled correctness-prediction AUROC can largely reflect problem difficulty rather than attempt-specific information, motivating question-only baselines and within-problem evaluation. Our work studies the analogous issue in runtime failure prediction for tool-using LLM agents. We evaluate repeated model–task executions across multiple agent benchmarks, behavioral predictors, published and released monitoring systems, and hidden-state probes, and then examine whether task-level and run-level information support different deployment decisions under fixed compute budgets.

paragraphs.en: Recent systems predict eventual success or failure from partial or complete agent trajectories. Cho et al. ( Cho et al., 2026 ) abstract trajectories into finite-state representations and report full-trajectory AUROC of 0.941 0.941 on Tau2-Bench telecom and 0.799 0.799 on SWE-agent. Shi et al. ( Shi et al., 2026 ) train predictors from partial trajectories and report 13–26% fewer execution steps while maintaining high prediction accuracy. Ruan et al. ( Ruan et al., 2026 ) instead use hidden-state probes to trigger early aborts, substantially reducing generated tokens on TextCraft and WebShop. Wang et al. ( Wang et al., 2026 ) propose FailFast–RestartSmart, which predicts failure from partial trajectories and restarts unpromising runs, reducing token usage by 14.6–20.4% at a 5% false-positive rate. Their training objective includes successful–failed pairs from the same task to control instance difficulty. Our study addresses a complementary evaluation question: how much of a monitor’s measured discrimination remains when successful and failed executions are compared within the same model–task unit.

( Raghu et al., 2026 ) show that AUROC does not assess whether predicted success probabilities remain meaningful across trajectory prefixes and propose a trajectory proper score. Their concern is calibration across time; ours is complementary. We instead ask what source of variation produces the observed discrimination by separating comparisons across model–task units from comparisons between successful and failed executions of the same unit. Prediction quality also does not guarantee useful intervention. Vasudev et al. ( Vasudev et al., 2026 ) show that a critic with strong offline failure-prediction performance can reduce task success when interventions disrupt trajectories that would otherwise succeed. paragraphs.en: Taken together, prior work shows that task difficulty is predictable, trajectories can contain failure-related information, and prediction-guided intervention can help or harm depending on how that information is used. What remains unclear is whether strong aggregate failure-prediction performance reflects task/model difficulty or genuine discrimination between successful and failed executions of the same model–task unit. We address this gap by decomposing pooled AUROC into within-unit and cross-unit components, evaluating predictors at online-computable prefixes, and testing whether run-level signals improve decisions under a fixed compute budget.
paragraphs.zh: 综合来看，先前的研究表明：任务难度是可预测的，轨迹可能包含与失败相关的信息，而基于预测的干预究竟能带来帮助还是造成危害，取决于这些信息的使用方式。 尚不明确的是，强大的整体失败预测性能究竟是反映了任务或模型本身的难度，还是真正能够区分同一模型–任务单元中成功执行与失败执行之间的差异。 我们通过将合并后的 AUROC 分解为单元内和跨单元两个组成部分、在可在线计算的词缀上评估预测指标，并测试运行层级的信号是否能在固定计算预算下改善决策，来解决这一研究空白。

sents.en: We address this gap by decomposing pooled AUROC into within-unit and cross-unit components, evaluating predictors at online-computable prefixes, and testing whether run-level signals improve decisions under a fixed compute budget.
sents.zh: 我们通过将合并后的 AUROC 分解为单元内和跨单元两个组成部分、在可在线计算的词缀上评估预测指标，并测试运行层级的信号是否能在固定计算预算下改善决策，来解决这一研究空白。

paragraphs.en: Following the Goal–Question–Metric (GQM) framework ( Basili et al., 1994 ) , the goal of our study is to analyze failure prediction for LLM agents for the purpose of understanding what reported predictive performance captures and whether the captured information supports useful deployment decisions, with respect to the distinction between task-level difficulty and run-level failure, from the perspective of researchers, tool builders, and practitioners, in the context of repeated-attempt agent benchmarks. We define a unit as a ( model , task ) (\text{model},\text{task}) pair. We use within-task AUROC as shorthand for discrimination within a fixed model–task unit, so both the task and acting model are held fixed. The following sections present the research questions (RQs) and details of each step of our study. Figure 1 summarizes the study design and the relationship between the three research questions.

paragraphs.en: ( Estimand ) What does pooled failure-prediction AUROC measure in benchmarks that record repeated attempts? We examine the contributions of within-unit and cross-unit comparisons and assess how much pooled discrimination is achievable without observing the current execution.

We therefore use the Latent Programming Horizons corpus ( Silva et al., 2026 ) as C4. paragraphs.en: Our main control is a predictor that never observes the current trajectory. The difficulty oracle assigns each run the failure rate of its unit. C3 supports an additional decomposition of task history and current-run information. paragraphs.en: To determine whether our findings are specific to our predictors, we also evaluate systems developed independently of our pipeline. We reimplement Automata ( Cho et al., 2026 ) because it reports the highest pooled AUROC in our survey ( 0.941 0.941 ) and is evaluated on SWE-agent (C1), allowing a same-corpus comparison. We first verify that our reconstruction matches its published SWE-agent result ( 0.799 0.799 ) on complete trajectories, then evaluate fixed prefixes under both A pool A_{\mathrm{pool}} and A within A_{\mathrm{within}} . The reconstruction uses the published activity-abstracted automaton with gradient boosting; additional implementation checks are reported in the supplementary material ( Anonymous, 2026 ) . We also evaluate released systems directly. EarlyEval ( Shi et al., 2026 ) is particularly relevant because it targets early failure prediction, reports 13 13 – 26 % 26\% fewer execution steps at 89 89 – 97 % 97\% accuracy, and requires no reconstruction. We run its released features on the pre-registered five-fold C2 split, where each of the 6,306 6{,}306 instances appears in test data once. Its step- 0 0 checkpoint predicts before the agent acts, providing a direct measure of pre-execution discrimination. We additionally evaluate the released one-class monitor of Dubey (2026) on the same C2 folds and run EarlyEval on C1’s three Llama-3 models to test whether the pattern extends across acting models.

paragraphs.en: Each probe uses GroupKFold grouped by task. Regularization strength is selected with a nested GroupKFold inside each training fold and never using test data. We compare these probes with a three-feature length baseline consisting of absolute token position, its logarithm, and assistant-turn count. We validate the probing pipeline in four ways: (1) we verify model loading with teacher-forced accuracy; (2) replay stored token identifiers directly; (3) compare the within-task AUROC estimator with an independent implementation to 10 − 9 10^{-9} agreement; and (4) evaluate positive and negative controls using an outcome-encoding feature, Gaussian noise, and shuffled labels. Numerical validation results are reported with the probe results.

paragraphs.en: All trajectory-based predictors satisfy the same deployment constraint: they may use only information available when the prediction is made. In particular, final trajectory length is unknown while an execution is still running. We therefore define checkpoints by absolute turn count rather than by a fraction of the completed trajectory. Fractional checkpoints depend on final length T T and therefore introduce information unavailable online. For Automata, we evaluate both its original fractional checkpoint and deployment-valid checkpoints based on observed turns and tokens, allowing us to quantify the effect of this leakage. Later checkpoints create a separate selection issue because runs that terminate early disappear from evaluation. To distinguish increasing predictive signal from changing cohort composition, we additionally evaluate a fixed C1 cohort containing only trajectories that reach at least ten turns, so the same runs are compared across early checkpoints.

paragraphs.en: Answer to RQ1. Pooled AUROC is dominated by comparisons between different model–task units. In our corpora, same-unit comparisons contribute no more than 6.8 × 10 − 4 6.8\times 10^{-4} of the pair mass. As a result, a predictor can achieve high pooled AUROC by identifying difficult tasks without distinguishing successful from failed runs of the same task. This is visible in the difficulty oracle, which reaches pooled AUROC 0.9454 0.9454 on C1 while remaining at chance ( 0.5000 0.5000 ) within task. Pooled AUROC therefore does not by itself establish run-level failure discrimination.
paragraphs.zh: RQ1 的答案。 合并 AUROC 主要由不同模型–任务单元之间的比较所主导。 在我们的语料库中，同一单元内的比较对成对质量的贡献不超过 6.8 × 10⁻⁴。 因此，预测器可以通过识别困难任务来实现较高的合并 AUROC，而无需区分同一任务中成功与失败的运行。 这一点在难度神谕中可见一斑：它在 C1 上达到了 0.9454 的合并 AUROC，而在任务内部则仍停留在随机水平（0.5000）。 因此，合并 AUROC 本身并不能证明具备运行级别的失败识别能力。

Thus, the weak within-task results are not explained by an incapable probe. paragraphs.en: Two factors explain much of the variation across corpora: trajectory depth and acting-model capability.
paragraphs.zh: 有两个因素可以解释不同语料库之间的大部分差异：轨迹深度和智能体模型的能力。

paragraphs.en: First, run-level signal increases with depth. On a fixed C1 cohort of 63,657 63{,}657 traces that all reach at least ten turns, within-task AUROC rises from 0.509 0.509 at one turn to 0.598 0.598 at ten, showing that the increase is not caused by survivor selection. Training directly for same-unit ranking improves early discrimination only modestly, reaching 0.526 0.526 , 0.535 0.535 , and 0.547 0.547 at one, three, and five turns, still far below the intervention requirements in Section 6.3 . This depth dependence helps reconcile our findings with FailFast–RestartSmart ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , which reports effective failure-triggered termination on SWE-bench Verified but suppresses alarms during the first 20 20 steps and augments terminal supervision with intermediate test-progress signals. A similar but weaker depth-dependent pattern appears in Bulut ( Bulut, 2026 ) : their main reconstructed hidden-state probe remains near chance within problem across checkpoints, while a post-hoc problem-centered probe recovers modest within-problem signal at later positions. Together, these results suggest that actionable run-specific information may become more available as trajectories develop, although its strength depends on the task, model, and representation.

paragraphs.en: Our results separate task-level predictability from run-level predictability. Pooled AUROC is dominated by cross-unit comparisons, allowing predictors that never observe the current run to achieve strong aggregate performance; for example, a task-difficulty scorer reaches 0.9454 0.9454 pooled AUROC while remaining at 0.5000 0.5000 within task. In contrast, early within-unit discrimination is consistently weak across the monitors and probes we evaluate, and the signal that does emerge tends to appear later and for weaker acting models. This distinction matters operationally: task-level information supports compute allocation, whereas run-level information is required for deciding whether to stop an ongoing execution. Under fixed token budgets, allocation outperforms abort-only strategies, while the monitor does not improve throughput.

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we examined what failure-prediction performance measures for LLM agents and whether those predictions support useful deployment decisions. Using benchmarks with repeated attempts of the same model-task unit, we separated task-level discrimination from discrimination between successful and failed runs of the same task. We evaluated run-blind baselines, trajectory predictors, hidden-state probes, and published and released failure-prediction systems, and then used replay experiments to study the consequences for compute allocation.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们研究了大语言模型智能体的故障预测性能指标，以及这些预测是否有助于做出有效的部署决策。 通过使用包含同一模型-任务单元重复尝试的基准测试，我们将任务层面的区分能力与同一任务中成功运行和失败运行之间的区分能力分离开来。 我们评估了“运行无关”的基线模型、轨迹预测器、隐藏状态探测器以及已发表和公开的故障预测系统，随后通过重播实验研究这些方法对计算资源分配的影响。

paragraphs.en: Our results show that strong pooled AUROC can largely reflect differences between units, and in particular differences in task difficulty, rather than information about the current run. More than 99.93 % 99.93\% of the positive–negative pairs underlying pooled AUROC compare runs from different units, allowing predictors that never observe the current trajectory to achieve strong pooled performance while remaining near chance within task. Early within-task discrimination is generally weak across the evaluated predictors and monitoring systems, although the signal becomes stronger later in execution and is more visible for weaker acting models.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究结果表明，较高的合并 AUROC 值主要能反映不同单元之间的差异，尤其是任务难度的差异，而非当前运行次数的相关信息。 在构成合并 AUROC 的正负样本对中，超过 99.93% 的对比涉及来自不同单元的运行次数，这使得从未观察到当前轨迹的预测模型也能实现较高的合并性能，同时其任务内表现仍接近随机水平。 在所有评估的预测模型和监控系统中，任务早期的区分能力普遍较弱，尽管在执行后期这种信号会增强，并且在表现较弱的模型中更为明显。

paragraphs.en: Overall, our study shows that failure-prediction evaluation should distinguish task-level predictability from run-level predictability. We recommend reporting within-task AUROC and the same-unit pair weight alongside pooled AUROC, evaluating predictors only at prefixes available during execution, and comparing run-level intervention policies against task-level allocation baselines. Doing so makes clear what information a failure predictor captures and whether that information supports the deployment decision for which the predictor is intended.
paragraphs.zh: 总体而言，我们的研究表明，故障预测评估应当区分任务级可预测性与运行级可预测性。 我们建议，在报告汇总 AUROC 的同时，也应报告任务内的 AUROC 和相同单元配对权重；仅在执行期间可用的前缀上评估预测模型，并将运行级干预策略与任务级分配基线进行比较。 这样做可以明确故障预测模型捕捉了哪些信息，以及这些信息是否支持该模型所预期的部署决策。

sents.en: Overall, our study shows that failure-prediction evaluation should distinguish task-level predictability from run-level predictability.
sents.zh: 总体而言，我们的研究表明，故障预测评估应当区分任务级可预测性与运行级可预测性。

sents.en: We recommend reporting within-task AUROC and the same-unit pair weight alongside pooled AUROC, evaluating predictors only at prefixes available during execution, and comparing run-level intervention policies against task-level allocation baselines.
sents.zh: 我们建议，在报告汇总 AUROC 的同时，也应报告任务内的 AUROC 和相同单元配对权重；仅在执行期间可用的前缀上评估预测模型，并将运行级干预策略与任务级分配基线进行比较。

sents.en: Doing so makes clear what information a failure predictor captures and whether that information supports the deployment decision for which the predictor is intended.
sents.zh: 这样做可以明确故障预测模型捕捉了哪些信息，以及这些信息是否支持该模型所预期的部署决策。
